text: with regular glucocor- ticoid therapy.7,8 Patients with non-salt-losing congenital adrenal hyper- plasia may be adequately managed with glucocorticoids alone, and in mild late-onset forms a single dose daily in the late evening (when its suppressive effect on ACTH production is greatest) may be sufficient. In adults who do not require mineralocorticoid treatment betamethasone or dexamethasone may be useful because of their lack of mineralocorticoid actions. Surgical correction may be necessary in females with mas- culinised external genitalia. Giving a glucocorticoid to pregnant women whose offspring are considered at risk has been tried in an attempt to prevent virilisation:3 dexa- methasone is preferred to hydrocortisone because of a lack of placental degradation.4 1. Corneal graft rejection Corticosteroids are the mainstay of postoperative prophy- laxis and treatment of corneal graft rejection.1 Topical and subconjunctival corticosteroids are widely used, but in acute rejection episodes involving the endothelium sys- temic therapy is usually necessary.
